uncited: **Inputs:** Raw 3D volume data (intensity values per voxel).
**Outputs:** Classified volume (voxel labels) and a color/opacity map for each class.
*   **Slice Entropy List:** List of slice indices sorted by descending entropy.
*   **Training Set:** List of voxels selected by the user, each tagged with a class label.
*   **Feature Vector:** 5-dimensional vector per voxel: $[I, G, A_X, A_Y, A_Z]$.
Calculate the image entropy for every slice in the X, Y, and Z directions.
Sort these slices in descending order of entropy.
Present the three selected slices in a GUI.
The user draws free-form boundaries around groups of voxels on these slices to select training samples.
Average the intensities of the 8 neighbors in the Y-Z plane: $(x, y\pm1, z\pm1), (x, y\pm1, z), (x, y, z\pm1)$.
Average the intensities of the 8 neighbors in the X-Z plane.
Train an SN-SVM classifier using the user-selected training voxels and their extracted 5D features.
Use a one-vs-one scheme for multi-class problems.
*   **Boundary Voxels:** Neighbor averaging and gradient calculation require handling volume boundaries.

*   **Time Complexity:** Dominated by feature extraction ($O(N)$ where $N$ is total voxels) and SVM classification ($O(N \cdot M)$ or similar depending on SVM implementation, where $M$ is training samples).
Entropy calculation is $O(S)$ where $S$ is number of slices.
*   **Memory Complexity:** Requires storing the volume, feature vectors for all voxels ($5 \times N$), and the trained SVM model.
